milestone.title: raul keybind overhaul v2: diagnostics, multiple bindings, profile export, data-driven help

intent.outcome: raul's keybind system is fully user-extensible: users can rebind any action in master-plan/config.json, define multiple keys per action (e.g. close-tab on both ctrl+w and ctrl+shift+t), see what they've changed via mp config show keybinds, and export a clean TOML profile fragment for editing. Bad config (invalid combo, conflicting bindings) is reported via tracing warns, not panics. The help overlay and footer are entirely data-driven from the Keybinds struct — adding a new action updates the help text automatically.

problem.description: M138 (v1) replaces the Event enum and adds a Keybinds struct + parser, but the binding for each action is a single combo (one field, one string). Users who want to bind close-tab to both ctrl+w AND ctrl+shift+t (herdr supports this via BindingConfig::One | Many with untagged serde) cannot. Users who fat-finger a config value and break their config have no clear diagnostic (herdr's validated_keybinds() returns prefix_diag + keybind_diags and uses fallback + warn). Users who want to see exactly what they've changed from defaults have to diff the entire config — herdr's local_keybindings_profile_toml() writes back a clean fragment with only user-displaced defaults. Without these, keybind config is fragile: easy to break, hard to inspect, hard to extend.

in_scope: Make Keybinds fields Vec<BindingConfig> (or one BindingConfig that's a One-or-Many untagged enum) so a single action can have multiple keys. Test covers serializing/deserializing both forms.
Keybinds::resolve returns the right action for any of the bound combos (first match wins; documented)

Config diagnostics: validated_keybinds() returns a Vec<Diagnostic> with a human-readable message per bad entry (invalid combo, unparseable value). Raul logs warnings and falls back to default per field, never crashes on bad config.

Keybinds::local_keybindings_profile_toml() returns a TOML string containing only the user-displaced defaults (so the user can copy it into a clean config and edit). Tests: round-trip preserves displaced entries, drops default-disabled entries, preserves partial displacements.

Help overlay and footer are entirely data-driven: iterate Keybinds struct to produce the help table; no hand-edited text strings in render.rs. Add a test that asserts the help text reflects every bound action with a stable, formatted key display (e.g. 'Ctrl+W' not 'ctrl+w').
Documented conflict policy: when two actions bind the same key, last-one-wins (order in the config file). Documented in Keybinds::load_from_config docs and a doc-test.
Tests for all the above: serialization, deserialization, conflict resolution, profile export round-trip, help-text generation, diagnostics on bad input
out_of_scope: User-level config override (~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml) — separate concern, defer until v1+v2 are stable
Indexed bindings (1..9 N-th item) — only add if a concrete use case appears
Custom commands (user-defined key -> shell command) — herdr has them; we may want them later but not in v2
Live keybind reload (mp config set keybinds.* while raul is running) — would require file watching; defer
Keybind UI inside raul (instead of editing the config file) — that's M140

acceptance_criteria.description: A single action can be bound to multiple keys via TOML array syntax: close_tab = ['ctrl+w', 'ctrl+shift+t']. Pressing either key triggers the action. The deserializer handles both One(String) and Many(Vec<String>) via untagged serde.

Reuses M138's Vec<KeyCombo> per action and the v1 help_entries (HelpEntry::keys_display already joins with ', ' for multi-binding display). acceptance_criteria.description: Bad config (invalid combo string, unparseable JSON value) does not crash raul: a tracing warn is emitted identifying the field and the bad value, and the affected action falls back to its default. Tests cover: empty string, garbage string, valid-looking but unparseable key name, conflicting bindings (two actions on the same key — resolve() picks the FIRST match in fixed field-declaration order; a warning is emitted, last-applied semantics are NOT used because serde_json object iteration order is not stable).

acceptance_criteria.description: v2 help behavior: when an action has MULTIPLE bindings (the v2 addition over M138), the help-overlay entry lists ALL of them in a stable order (e.g. 'Close Tab    Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+T'), not just the first. The base data-driven-help invariant (help generated from Keybinds, no hardcoded key lists in render.rs) is already pinned by M138 AC-05; this AC specifically covers the v2 multi-binding display so M139 doesn't merely re-assert M138's behavior. Test: bind an action to two combos, render help, assert both appear comma-separated.

work_packages.name: Profile export + data-driven help

steps.action: In crates/raul/src/tui/keybinds.rs, change each Keybinds field to use BindingConfig (untagged serde over One(String) | Many(Vec<String>)) so a single action can be bound to multiple keys. Update resolve() to return the first matching action across all bound combos.
steps.done_when: TOML `close_tab = ['ctrl+w', 'ctrl+shift+t']` deserializes and both keys trigger the action; One(String) form still works.

steps.action: Add validated_keybinds() in keybinds.rs that returns (Vec<Diagnostic>, Keybinds). Diagnostics identify the field and the bad value. load_from_config falls back to Default per field when diagnostics are non-empty, emitting a tracing warn. Documented conflict policy: last-one-wins (order in the config file).
steps.done_when: Bad config (invalid combo, unparseable value, conflicting bindings) does not crash raul; warnings emitted; per-field fallback works.

steps.action: Implement Keybinds::local_keybindings_profile_toml() returning a TOML string with only user-displaced defaults. Round-tripping it through load_from_config produces the same Keybinds; default values do not appear in the output; default-disabled bindings (the user removed them) do not appear.
steps.done_when: Round-trip tests pass; displaced entries preserved; default entries dropped; default-disabled entries dropped.

steps.action: When an action has MULTIPLE bindings (v2), the help-overlay entry under crates/raul/src/tui/render/ lists ALL of them in a stable formatted display (e.g. Ctrl+W). Builds on M138 single-binding help — do not re-litigate single-binding generation.
steps.done_when: Help text is data-driven; formatted key display is correct; grep test asserts no hand-edited key lists in render.rs.

findings.description: Hand-written TOML profile round-trip (local_keybindings_profile_toml/load_from_profile_toml) silently dropped bindings whose combo char is '#' (naive split_once('#') treated it as a comment) or '"' (trim_matches over-stripped), and the array form mis-split on a quoted ','-key. Fixed: quote-aware comment stripping + proper basic-string escape/unescape + quote-aware array split; new round-trip test pins '#'/'"'/',' keys.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: Undeclared drift: AC-02 described conflict resolution as 'last wins' but resolve() picks the FIRST match in fixed field-declaration order (serde_json object iteration order is not stable, so last-applied semantics would be fragile). AC-02 text corrected to state first-match-in-fixed-order; behavior unchanged.
